key_insight: EM-DETR combines heterogeneous medical imaging datasets with example-based grounding to improve multi-domain lesion detection.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more adaptable computer-aided detection across chest X-rays and mammography, but clinical benefit remains unestablished.
method: Integrates datasets annotated for anatomical structures and abnormalities.
Uses student–teacher training to reconcile heterogeneous labels and mitigate catastrophic forgetting.
Extends example-based EM-DETR for joint learning across domain-specific datasets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports image-level AUC gains exceeding 1 percentage point over prior state of the art for four chest X-ray findings and mAP50 gains of 2–3 percentage points over single-dataset EM-DETR in chest X-rays and mammography.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, external validation, or prospective clinical evaluation, limiting assessment of real-world generalizability.
paper_title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
